text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday:

- The Bank for Internaitonal Settlements informed on Monday on its gold trade activities with the Nazis. Between 1939 and 1945, some 13.5 tonnes of gold were transfered from the accounts of the Reichsbank, of which 3.7 tonnes was identified as 'conquested gold'.

- The Lichtenstein parliament will have to suggest a new chairman of the Administrative Court to Prince Hans Adam II on Wednesday. The prince's refusal of the first candidate marked yet another stage in the confronation course between parliament and the monarchy.
- Some 150 farmers demonstrated against gene technology in Basle on Monday. The organizers expected at least a crowd of 2,000 protesters.

- Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti told Swiss national radio that he supported the Eizenstat report's proposal to hold an international historians' conference to look into gold trade and other business activities between neutral states and the Nazis. Cotti rejected U.S. Senator D'Amato's demand to renegotiate the Washington Treaty from 1946.
- The French and Italian speaking regions in Switzerland count more graduates from university (9.6 percent of the population) than the German speaking cantons (5.9 percent).

- The proponants of the so-called Swissmetro, a high-speed underground train connection between major Swiss towns, may soon get support by a large international group which will accquire a stake in the company.
